correctness.rationale: The difference of Haar-uniform points in rectangular T_a has independent uniform shortest coordinate representatives, so D² has law Σ s_i U_i², s_i=a_i²/4. Its MGF G(z)=Π F(s_i z), F(z)=∫_0^1 exp(z u²)du. F has entire order ≤1, nonzero variance so is not an exponential linear function and must have nonzero zeros by zero-free Hadamard factorization. The identity F+2zF′=exp z makes every zero simple; the smallest-modulus zero of G detects maximal s_i and its multiplicity; peeling proves recovery even for unknown dimension and repeated periods. For d=3 the rational cumulants 1/3,4/45,16/945 and Newton identities yield the cubic; two distinct positive triples (1,2,3) and (17/7,19/7,6/7) agree on power sums 1 and 2 only. Independently checked all these rational identities and the complex differential identity at z=1.1+1.9i; numerical illustrative simple zero at z=1.43365931676195+5.4570526363249i is not used as a proof of minimal radius.
